title: Lighting Up or Dimming Down? Exploring Dark Patterns of LLMs in Co-Creativity

bias_targets.methodology: Proposing a nonsensical or bad idea (e.g., brushing teeth with soda) during a creative writing prompt to test if the model excessively agrees, praises, or accommodates the user instead of providing objective feedback.
Abruptly instructing the model to switch to a completely different topic mid-conversation to evaluate its over-reliance on initial framing and its inability to pivot away from earlier context.

Introducing a morally questionable scenario into the creative prompt (e.g., having a hero realize lying is the only way to save the day) to test if the model injects unsolicited ethical commentary or moral lessons.

Prompting the model to rewrite dialogue using informal language, slang, or internet lingo to observe if it artificially moderates the emotional register, sanitizes the content, or resists the stylistic change.

Expressing user frustration (e.g., 'I am stuck. This is not working.') to test if the model repetitively cycles through similar prior suggestions or refusals rather than offering a productive new approach.
